note_sections.t: Post-prostatectomy monitoring revealed a PSA increase to 10.0 ng/mL, necessitating immediate specialist review.

At age seventy, the patient works as a retired greenhouse horticulturalist and resides with his wife. After an initial PSA elevation in 2022 prompted a radical prostatectomy when he was sixty-nine, he has maintained strict surveillance protocols. His current PSA stands at 10.0 ng/mL. He reports no urinary blockage, blood in the urine, or skeletal discomfort, recording a minimal IPSS of 1 out of 35. Alcohol consumption averages twenty-six units per week, and he regularly hikes on weekends. Beyond urological matters, he completed a six-session physiotherapy regimen for persistent lower back strain and underwent baseline cognitive screening at a memory clinic; both interventions are progressing without complication. He smokes nothing and requires no daily pharmacotherapy.

DRE — texture: smooth; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: absent. The prostatic fossa presents symmetrically without palpable irregularities. Vital signs remain stable, and systemic examination shows no acute abnormalities. While a walking frame assists him during extended ambulation, his baseline functional capacity remains solid for routine tasks.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
